author: Kyle Powell
title: Another poor road effort sinks Sabres in Philadelphia - NewsBreak
text:
By Kyle Powell ,
4 hours ago
Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (WGR Sports Radio 550) - The Buffalo Sabres cannot get out of their own way.
Winners of two-straight games coming in, a six-game road trip kicked off tonight with another porous display of defense and passive shooting moments as the Philadelphia Flyers took care of business on home ice inside Xfinity Mobile Arena.
Jason Zucker opened the scoring, on a powerplay, for a second-consecutive game. Zucker's eighth goal of the season was set up by a nice centering pass from Josh Doan.
Unlike last game, the opposition struck back, and retaliated in a big way. The next three first-period goals belonged to the Flyers. All three scores came during the midway point of the stanza.
First, it was forward Travis Konecny's point shot through traffic that tied things at one. Buffalo challenged for goaltender interference, but extra video evidence wasn't enough to support the claim. This, of course, led to a Philadelphia powerplay.
On that powerplay, the Flyers benefitted from a wild deflection. Forward Trevor Zegras' cross-ice pass went in the net, and behind Colten Ellis after caroming off the leg of Ryan McLeod. That gave Philadelphia its first lead of the night, at 2-1.
21-seconds later, a failed clearing attempt ended up in the back of the Sabres' net. Doing the damage was Flyers forward Bobby Brink, who crashed the net hard and cashed in on a rebound from linemate Noah Cates' shot.
Philadelphia then fortified its 3-1 lead just 1:45 into the second period. Cates and Brink traded places on the scoresheet, as this time Cates finished a scoring play from Brink to make it 4-1.
The Sabres were, temporarily, able to stop the barrage at the 11:48 mark of the second. Bowen Byram connected for his fifth goal in the last 11 games to cut the deficit in half, 4-2.
The two-goal deficit lasted all of 55-seconds, before Philadelphia extended its lead to three again. Forward Owen Tippett was left alone long enough to bat the rebound from his initial shot into the net himself.
The blue and gold also lost the services of captain Rasmus Dahlin with 3:10 to play in the middle stanza. Dahlin was handed a five-minute boarding major, and a game misconduct for this hit on Zegras.
It was all over but the shouting in the third. Zach Benson looked to have finally scored his first goal of the season, but it was taken off the board by an offside challenge by Philadelphia.
The Sabres still have just two wins away from KeyBank Center in 2025-26. Neither of which were settled in regulation.
